subject: HelixPay: slotting strategy & fallback clauses for dedicated commitment
messages:
From: Devon Lee <devon@helixpay.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-09-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: HelixPay dedicated - slotting & fallback questions

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the deck yesterday — HelixPay is excited about the dedicated path. Before we lock in numbers with procurement we need clarity on two operational points that will affect commercial terms: slotting (how bursts are slotted across the reserved pool) and automatic fallbacks (what you route to when the committed pool hits capacity).

High level asks:
- If we buy a 5k-token-commit (monthly), how do you define a "burst slot" and how is it charged vs sustained usage?
- If the dedicated pool saturates for a short window (e.g., 10-15 minutes), what's the default fallthrough? Does traffic go to a cheaper quantized variant or to hosted best-effort?
- Are there soft pre-warm guarantees for advertised burst windows? If so, what are the limitations (max concurrent sessions per burst)?

Procurement is asking for specific guardrails we can put in the MSA (e.g., a max 30-minute continuous fallback window before credits apply, or a throttling behavior).

I attached a small sample of our traffic shape (we'll send a fuller CSV if helpful). Can your pre-sales team sketch a slotting/fallback playbook so we can align legal?

Thanks,
Devon Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, HelixPay
devon@helixpay.com

Attachment: helixpay_burst_sample.csv (CSV stub)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-09-19T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: HelixPay dedicated - slotting & fallback questions

Devon — thanks, this is exactly the sort of detail that makes pricing and SLAs predictable. I have a couple quick clarifying Qs before Marissa and Marcus draft a formal playbook:

1) Traffic basics
- Current p95 latency target for production (ms)?
- Typical concurrency (peak concurrent sessions) and whether those are long-lived sessions or short request/response calls.
- Token mix: average prompt length (tokens), average response length (tokens), and heavy-tail p99 response length if available.

2) Burst shape and frequency
- Typical burst duration (minutes) and daily frequency (how many burst events/day).
- % of daily traffic in top 1% of minutes (helps us size transient headroom).

3) Acceptable fallback behaviors (choose any preferred option)
- Option A: Route to a quantized-compatible model (same quality band, lower cost).
- Option B: Route to hosted best-effort instance (no single-tenant SLA, lower cost, potential cold-start).
- Option C: Queueing with graceful 503 backoff and guaranteed retry window.

4) Penalty/credit expectations (for procurement) — are you looking for credits per minute beyond X fallback minutes per month, or per-event guarantees?

If you can reply with those bullets and attach the fuller CSV, I will have Marissa produce a slotting sketch (how we assign burst slots to tenant subpools) and Marcus add the kernel/instance mix recommendation.

— Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Devon Lee <devon@helixpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-09-29T15:26:00Z
Subject: Re: HelixPay dedicated - slotting & fallback questions

Thanks for the details, Devon — this gives us enough to draft a slotting/fallback playbook and a preliminary instance mix. High-level proposal below (we'll convert to short doc + SLA redline):

Slotting and burst accounting
- Definition: a burst slot = contiguous 1-minute window where tenant consumption exceeds their sustained baseline. We allocate transient burst capacity as 2x sustained tokens/sec across a configurable pool of 'burst tokens' from the committed quota.
- Accounting: burst tokens are debited against the monthly commitment at the same unit rate; overage beyond committed burst reserve will be charged at the overage rate in the MSA.
- Headroom guardrail: we recommend reserving 12% of committed capacity as short-duration headroom for promo spikes (configurable during contracting).

Fallback behavior (per your preference)
- Default for payments-critical endpoints: Option A — route to quantized-compatible variant (same model family, int8/4 quantization) with pre-warmed slots for first N concurrent sessions (we propose N=40 per region).
- Non-critical batch endpoints: Option C — queueing with exponential backoff, guaranteed retry window of 10 minutes.
- If dedicated pool remains saturated > 30 contiguous minutes for the tenant: trigger automatic credit calculation and escalation to SRE/CS. Crediting formula: minutes_over_threshold * (committed_rate_per_minute * credit_factor). We'll provide a draft clause — happy to align on the cap procurement asked for (10%).

Recommended fleet mix and sizing assumptions (quick sketch)
- Kernel/instance mix: for your token mix and p99 sizes we recommend a mixed pool: 60% A100-80GB-equivalent (for long p99 responses), 40% A40-class/4-bit optimized nodes for high-concurrency, low-latency endpoints.
- KV cache assumptions: assume ~0.6MB per active session KV occupancy for long-lived sessions; plan for KV pressure during burst by reserving 20% extra GPU RAM headroom in the slotting pool.
- Session pinning: use session affinity for 75% of interactive sessions to avoid KV replication costs, allow best-effort affinity for streaming endpoints to improve p95.
- Quantization sensitivity: we will run a validation sweep (A100 int8 / int4) on a 1k-sample from your p99 responses; worst-case BLEU/QA regression thresholds should be agreed (we'll propose <1.5% quality delta for payments-critical endpoints).

Operational playbook items to include in the MSA/Annex
- Defined burst windows and notification SLA (30s SLA to notify of active burst event).
- Fallback activation rules and automatic fallback timeout (default 30 minutes).
- Credit calculation sample and 10% cap option.
- Pre-warm reservation count and process for temporary increases (notify 48h for sustained increases >2 hours).

Next steps
1) Steph/Marissa to produce a 2-page slotting diagram + sample MSA redline for procurement by Oct 3.
2) Marcus to run quick quantization sensitivity run on the attached CSV and return accuracy delta and token-rate benchmarks by Oct 2.
3) Devon to confirm whether HelixPay accepts the 12% headroom recommendation or proposes an alternative percent.

I'll attach SLA draft and the CSV for your legal and infra teams.

— Marissa
